data.title: Tesla Semi Wins Top Gear Tech Award
data.description:
Top Gear has awarded the Tesla Semi its Tech Award, praising the electric truck as a reminder of Tesla at its best.

Influential UK-based auto media house Top Gear has recognised the Tesla Semi with the Tech Award. In the 2027 edition of the US Car Awards, the electric truck is described as Tesla at its brilliant best. According to Top Gear:

“One thing is for sure: this is the version of Tesla we want to see. The version focused on making important vehicles that serve normal people brilliantly. Amid all the recent noise, it’s become all too easy to forget what this company is capable of at its brilliant best. The Semi is a potent reminder.”

Tesla refreshed the Semi in September with a light bar at the front, electric steering, a heat pump, and many more changes “under the hood.”

The automaker offers two versions: Standard and Long Range, with 325-mile and 500-mile driving ranges respectively when fully loaded. The Semi can even travel further its advertised range when carrying lighter loads.

It can also charge at 1.2 MW, allowing it to go from 0 to 60 percent in just 30 minutes with a Megacharger.

Tesla produces the Semi in Nevada, with a capacity of 50,000 trucks per year. Tesla will start shipping to Europe in 2027.

A pre-production Tesla Semi caught fire days ago, shutting down a California highway for hours. No cause has been given for the blaze.

data.title: F1 champion Nico Rosberg praises Tesla FSD as “life changing”
data.description:
For the second time in less than a week another Formula 1 World Champion has praised Tesla’s self-driving technology, with Nico Rosberg sharing his experience just days after Damon Hill took a driverless Cybercab ride in Austin.

According to a LinkedIn post shared Friday, Rosberg has been testing Tesla’s Full Self-Driving (FSD) (Supervised) in a Cybertruck while attending meetings around San Francisco.

The 2016 F1 World Champion and founder of Rosberg Ventures described the experience as life-changing, saying the technology has made his busy schedule easier to manage.

“I’ve been test-driving the Tesla Cybertruck with Full Self-Driving around San Francisco… and it’s been LIFE-CHANGING!,” he said. (via EVWire)

Rosberg explained that he had back-to-back meetings across the city, but using FSD made his commutes less tiring and helped him arrive feeling more focused. He even managed to spend some quality time with his wife during one of the drives.

“My whole racing career, I was the one in control behind the wheel. But I’m now fully willing to hand over control!!” Rosberg wrote.

His comments come shortly after fellow F1 champion Damon Hill, who won the championship in 1996, experienced Tesla’s Cybercab in Austin following the United States Grand Prix.

Unlike Rosberg’s supervised Cybertruck experience, Hill’s ride was driverless, with the former champion sharing a 79-second video of the experience.

Rosberg added that Europe is falling behind in assisted-driving technology and called for faster progress in bringing these systems to the region. Currently only 10 EU countries have approved FSD following the provisional approval in the Netherlands earlier this year. To appease regulators in the region, Tesla also renamed FSD Tesla Assisted Driving.

data.title: Volkswagen Suspends Development of Electric Golf Amid Deepening Financial Troubles
data.description:
Volkswagen has suspended development work on its upcoming all-electric Golf at its Wolfsburg headquarters, putting one of its key future models on hold amid ongoing delays to its electric vehicle plans.

According to a Volkswagen statement released Friday, the company is temporarily pausing work on the ID. Golf until it can securely accommodate the necessary investments.

The decision comes as Volkswagen pushes ahead with plans to eliminate 100,000 jobs and close up to four German plants, following its largest quarterly loss in more than a decade.

In an internal memo obtained by Reuters, Thomas Schaefer, CEO of Volkswagen’s volume brands, acknowledged the importance of the Golf to the company and its Wolfsburg operations.

“I know what the Golf means for Volkswagen and for Wolfsburg. That’s why this decision was really not an easy one for us,” Schaefer said. He added, “We simply can’t afford this work right now.”

The Wolfsburg plant is €300 million (C$470M/US$336M) behind its cost-cutting target, although the facility is not among those facing possible closure.

Despite the suspension, Volkswagen’s works council insists the ID. Golf’s launch will not be delayed, saying the company intends to recover the lost development time.

The ID. Golf is expected to use Volkswagen’s next-generation SSP software architecture, which has already experienced delays from its original 2026 launch target.

Volkswagen’s financial results highlight the pressure facing its EV business. The Volkswagen Passenger Cars operating margin fell to 1.3% through September, with operating profit dropping to €813 million from €1,476 million.

In Canada, Volkswagen currently offers the ID.4 and ID. Buzz, with the ID. Tiguan confirmed to replace the ID.4 later in 2027. The automaker has not confirmed Canadian availability for the ID. Golf.

data.title: Tesla launches new 0% financing plan and discounts in China
data.description:
Tesla has launched a new 0% financing plan in China, lowering down payment requirements for the Model 3 and Model Y alongside new limited-time discounts on both vehicles.

According to Tesla China’s official promotions page, the offers are available for orders placed between October 30 and November 30, 2026.

The new financing plan allows buyers to put down as little as 39,900 yuan (C$8,380), compared to the previous minimum of 79,900 yuan (C$16,780).

Buyers can choose between traditional 0% financing for up to five years or a new flexible plan offering lower monthly payments with a final balloon payment.

For example, the entry-level Model 3 starts at 235,500 yuan (C$49,455), before a 10,000 yuan (C$2,100) discount, with monthly payments of up to about 2,429 yuan (C$510).

However, that lower monthly payment comes with a final payment of 39,900 yuan (C$8,380) after five years. Without the balloon payment, monthly payments are up to about 3,094 yuan (C$650).

The Model Y receives a smaller 4,000 yuan (C$840) discount, with monthly payments of up to about 2,995 yuan (C$629) under the flexible financing plan.

Meanwhile, the larger six-seat Model Y L is also included, with a minimum down payment of 59,900 yuan (C$12,580) and monthly payments of up to about 3,920 yuan (C$823).

In Canada, financing remains considerably more expensive. Tesla’s Canadian Model 3 configurator showed a 5.21% APR example over 96 months as of October 2, up from 4.99% previously. And with the Bank of Canada increasing interest rates yesterday for the first time in 3 years, we expect Tesla’s rates to increase again on November 1.

data.title: Toyota and Waymo Set to Launch Autonomous bZ4X in Japan
data.description:
Toyota and Waymo have announced the next phase of their autonomous driving partnership, with plans to begin testing a fleet of self-driving Toyota bZ4X vehicles in Japan in 2027.

According to Toyota’s announcement on Friday, the companies will begin testing and validating the vehicles in Japan before expanding to the United Kingdom and other Waymo markets in subsequent years.

The vehicles will be manufactured at Toyota’s Takaoka plant in Toyota City, Aichi Prefecture, Japan, where both vehicle assembly and installation of Waymo’s autonomous driving hardware will take place.

The partnership will combine Toyota’s vehicle manufacturing expertise with Waymo’s Level 4 autonomous driving technology, which allows vehicles to operate without human intervention under specific conditions.

The modified bZ4X will also feature several upgrades designed for ride-hailing, including additional rear legroom, automatic doors, a power liftgate, and ambient lighting.

Waymo co-CEO Dmitri Dolgov said, “In areas where Waymo operates, we’ve demonstrated that we are up to 20x safer than human drivers when it comes to serious crash injuries.”

Beyond robotaxis, Toyota and Waymo will continue exploring how autonomous driving technology could eventually be integrated into personally owned Toyota vehicles.

The companies will also work with Woven by Toyota to explore how Waymo’s driving data and technology could improve road safety.

The announcement comes as Waymo continues expanding internationally, including plans to launch a robotaxi service in Toronto in 2028. The company is also pushing for approval in Alberta.

data.title: Tesla makes subtle change to Canadian Model 3 configurator amid order pause
data.description:
Tesla has made a small change to its Canadian Model 3 configurator, allowing customers to select the Premium trims again, although orders remain paused due to import quota restrictions.

According to a check of Tesla Canada’s website by Drive Tesla on Friday, the Model 3 Premium trims are no longer greyed out and can now be selected in the configurator as if you can purchase them again.

However, Tesla is still not accepting orders for either Model 3 Premium trim in Canada. Now instead of an order button, Tesla displays a “Get updates” button, allowing customers to sign up for notifications about the vehicle’s availability.

Tesla stopped accepting orders for the China-built Model 3 Premium on October 12, after the automaker said it had exhausted its allocation under Canada’s Chinese electric vehicle (EV) import quota.

Both Premium trims were affected by the pause, including the entry-level version that had been priced starting at $39,490 before orders were suspended.

Tesla Canada public policy executive Iain Myrans previously explained that Global Affairs Canada tells automakers in advance how many vehicles they can expect to import during a given period.

The configurator change also comes just days after Tesla briefly updated the Canadian Model 3 Premium Rear-Wheel Drive (RWD) specifications to match the U.S. built version.

Those specifications showed 584 kilometres of range and a 0-100 km/h acceleration time of 5.2 seconds, before Tesla reverted to the previous figures on Tuesday.

data.title: Tesla opens Keremeos Supercharger [British Columbia]
data.description:
Tesla has opened a new Supercharger in Keremeos, British Columbia, bringing online a project that first appeared on the company’s Supercharger roadmap more than two years ago.

Keremeos initially appeared on Tesla’s charging map in March 2024, with an opening targeted before that year ended. That timeline passed, and Tesla subsequently removed the proposed station from its Find Us page.

The town returned to the map in September 2025 as “In Development.” By early July 2026, Tesla had changed its status to “Under Construction,” alongside another B.C. project in Sicamous.

Just three months later and the station is now open. According to Tesla, the new Keremeos Superchager is located at the local Pharmasave (520 7th Avenue), with V4 posts and charging speeds up to 325 kW for compatible EVs.

Tesla drivers pay $0.28/kWh, while the drivers of other electric vehicles is $0.38/kWh when using their own NACS adapter.

Tesla also has several other Supercharger projects underway in B.C. Construction updates this month include Merritt on October 12 and Squamish on October 5, while a new Burnaby station has been under construction since July.

Keremeos follows three northern B.C. openings in late September, just over a month ago. Vanderhoof opened on September 21, followed by Terrace on September 22 and Prince Rupert on September 23.

data.title: Tesla Adds New Calm Mode to Robotaxi
data.description:
Tesla has introduced a new Calm Mode for Robotaxi passengers, adding another feature to its growing list of rider controls.

According to a video shared on X by Robotaxi rider Spencer (@scotsrule08), the new feature allows passengers to turn off the driving visualization during trips, with the main display instead showing a mostly dark screen and only basic trip information.

The video shows the display with an “Arriving soon” message and the passenger’s destination, along with instructions to “Tap display to exit quiet mode.”

The feature appears particularly useful for nighttime rides, when the bright driving visualization can be distracting for passengers trying to relax.

Not long after Scot’s video was posted, Tesla shared on X that Robotaxi now operates until 2 AM every day, also announcing the addition of Calm Mode. According to Tesla, the feature also “sets cabin lighting to a relaxing state.”

data.title: Telesat Reports Wider Q3 Loss, Delays Lightspeed to Mid-2028
data.description:
Telesat has reported a larger third-quarter loss while pushing back the global launch of its Lightspeed satellite network, a project Canada is backing as an alternative to Starlink.

According to Telesat’s financial results, revenue fell 20% to C$81 million in Q3 2026, compared with C$101 million a year earlier. Its net loss widened to C$157 million from C$121 million.

Adjusted earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization (EBITDA) dropped 74% to C$12 million, partly reflecting C$25 million in debt refinancing expenses.

Meanwhile, Telesat invested C$368 million in Lightspeed during the quarter, bringing its nine-month investment to C$705 million. Its LEO backlog stood at approximately C$5.6 billion.

During Thursday’s earnings call, Telesat President and CEO Dan Goldberg said global service is now expected around the end of Q2 2028, three months later than previously planned (via Via Satellite).

The delay reflects changes to Telesat’s launch schedule. Instead of using a dedicated SpaceX Falcon 9 launch for its first two satellites, the company plans to launch them aboard a third-party Falcon 9 mission in mid-2027.

Following roughly two months of testing, Telesat expects to begin launching 15 satellites per dedicated Falcon 9 mission, starting around September 2027.

Despite the revised schedule, Telesat still expects to begin high-latitude commercial service around the end of Q1 2028, including services for the Canadian military in the Arctic.

In August, Telesat also announced a C$2.7 billion agreement, including option periods, with Canada’s Defence Investment Agency whose milestone payments will principally fund an expansion of Lightspeed from 156 to 225 satellites.

data.title: Rogers expands satellite-to-mobile roaming to Japan, Australia and New Zealand
data.description:
Rogers has expanded its satellite-to-mobile service to three more international destinations, allowing its customers to stay connected in Japan, Australia and New Zealand when travelling outside traditional cellular coverage.

The expansion brings its international satellite-to-mobile roaming coverage to four countries, including the United States.

The service allows customers to send text messages and use supported apps such as WhatsApp, Messenger and X for messaging, along with Google Maps and AllTrails for navigation and AccuWeather for real-time weather information, in areas where traditional cellular networks are unavailable.

Rogers says more satellite-ready apps are on the way, although the company has not provided a timeline for their availability.

“Canadians want to stay connected wherever their travels take them. With satellite-to-mobile roaming in Japan, Australia and New Zealand, we’re extending coverage to more destinations around the world so customers can stay connected when travelling abroad,” said Mark Kennedy, Chief Technology Officer, Rogers.

The international satellite roaming service is included with Rogers Ultimate plans, eligible Roam Like Home options and select Travel Passes.

The expansion follows Rogers’ launch of satellite-to-mobile roaming in the United States earlier this year, when the company says it became the first and only Canadian carrier to offer the service south of the border.
